headline: Adopted updated tobacco regulations, effective July 15, 2026, including a cap on smoke shops and penalties for sales to minors.
summary: Speakers offered both support for and opposition to the proposed tobacco regulations, including changes to the 500-foot buffer. The regulations were then adopted, with an effective date of July 15, 2026.
decisions: Adopted the updated City of Worcester tobacco regulations, effective July 15, 2026, by a 4-0 vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Following discussion and approval of the effective date, the Chair revised the motion to accept the proposed tobacco regulations as presented, with an effective date of July 15, 2026. ... The motion passed unanimously.

plain_text:
WORCESTER BOARD OF HEALTH PUBLIC HEARING ON PROPOSED 
TOBACCO REGULATIONS 
Meeting Minutes  
July 13, 2026 
25 MEADE STREET, ROOM 109 1ST FLOOR. WORCESTER, MA 
 
1. Call to Order 
Chair Frances Anthes called the public hearing to order at 6:30 p.m. 
 
She stated the purpose of the hearing was to receive public comments on the proposed tobacco 
regulations for the City of Worcester. She noted that speakers would be called in the order they 
signed the speaker sign-in sheet, and that copies of the proposed regulations were available through 
the Worcester Division of Public Health and on the City's website. 
 
Rescheduling of the Public Hearing 
Chair Anthes explained that the public hearing had originally been scheduled for June 15, 2026, 
but was canceled because it was not posted within the timeframe required by the Massachusetts 
Open Meeting Law. The hearing was subsequently rescheduled for July 13, 2026. 
She then provided an overview of the Worcester Board of Health, its role, and authority, and 
introduced the members of the Board in attendance; 
• Michael Perotto, MS 
• Patrick Lowe, MD 
• Joseph Kaharo, PA-C 
• Frances Anthes, MSW, LICSW 
 
The following staff members also introduced themselves: 
• Alex Arriaga, Assistant Commissioner of Health and Human Services 
• Dr. Jennifer Bradford, Medical Director, Health and Human Services 
• Nikki Nixon, Interim Director of Public Health 
• Jennifer Nakijoba, Chief of Community Health 
 
Chair Anthes acknowledged Commissioner of Health and Human Services Seema Dixit and other 
attendees participating remotely via Teams. 
 
2. Public Hearing Procedures and Guidelines 
The Chair explained that if the Board did not vote on the proposed regulations during the hearing, 
the date of a meeting at which the regulations would be considered and voted upon would be 
announced. She further stated that the subsequent meeting would be open to the public, but 
additional public comment would not be accepted unless requested by a Board member for 
clarification. She said  that if adopted, the regulations would be made available through the
Worcester Division of Public Health, published in summary form in the Telegram & Gazette and 
on the City of Worcester's website within 14 days of adoption, and that the Board would vote on 
the regulations' effective date. 
 
Speakers were instructed to sign the speaker sign -in sheet, state their name and address before 
speaking, limit comments to the proposed regulations, and keep remarks to a two-minutes 
timeframe. Attendees were also advised that disruptive behavior would not be permitted and could 
result in removal from the hearing at the Chair's discretion. 
 
3. Opening of the Public Hearing 
The Chair requested a motion to open the public hearing. A motion was made by Board Member 
Michael Perotto and unanimously approved. 
Motion: To open the public hearing. Motion made by: Michael Perotto 
Vote: Unanimously approved. 
Summary of Written Public Comments 
The Chair summarized written comments submitted prior to the public hearing for the Board’s 
consideration. 
1. A nurse manager at a local community health center opposed removing the 500-foot buffer for 
smoking bars and permitting flavored tobacco products in smoking bars, citing public health 
concerns and the disproportionate impact of tobacco-related illness on vulnerable communities 
and youth. 
 
2. A representative of Philip Morris International recommended that future tobacco regulations 
be evidence -based, distinguish between combustible and non -combustible products, and 
include a public process for case-specific relief related to spacing and buffer requirements. The 
company also stated that its goal is a smoke -free future by encouraging adult smokers to 
transition to non-combustible alternatives while preventing youth access to tobacco products. 
 
3. The third written comment came from Meryl's Safe Haven who expressed  some support for 
the proposed regulations. They supported the proposed retail restrictions, retailer education 
and training requirements, accountability measures, and standardized penalties for violations.  
They, however, did not support removing the 500-foot buffer between businesses citing 
flavored tobacco and vaping products as a significant public health concern affecting youth. 
 
4. A Worcester resident expressed concern about youth vaping and urged the Board to strengthen 
enforcement against retailers selling vaping products.  
 
5. A reporter from the Worcester Guardian requested the rationale behind the proposed regulatory 
changes. 
 
6. A resident urged the Board to limit the number of smoke shop tobacco retail permits and to 
continue prohibiting the sale of tobacco products to individuals under the age of 21.
Additional Written Comments Received After the Deadline 
The Chair advised that five additional written comments were received after the established 
submission deadline but would nevertheless be shared. 
• City Council Vice Chair Khrystian E. King submitted comments supporting an exemption 
from the proposed 500 -foot buffer requirement for N oamesco, noting the business's 
compliance history and expressing support for local businesses. 
• Julius Kumah , co -owner of N oamesco submitted comments supporting the proposed 
regulations, stating they would strengthen Worcester's commercial districts and better 
serve the community, including allowing more downtown evening activities. 
• Yajaira Paulino,  co-owner of N oamesco also expressed support for the proposed 
regulations, stating that they appropriately balance public health objectives with 
responsible economic development. 
• Mayor Joseph M. Petty submitted comments supporting the proposed regulations while 
emphasizing the importance of balancing public health protections with equitable 
opportunities for small businesses and continued downtown economic development. 
 
• The Worcester Regional Chamber of Commerce submitted comments supporting the 
proposed regulations, stating they would protect public health while supporting 
Worcester's small business community. 
 
4. Public Testimony 
The Chair opened the floor for public comment. 
 Chris Banthin, a resident of Natick and representing the Public Health Advocacy Institute, 
spoke. He stated that nicotine addiction remains a leading preventable cause of disease and death 
and cited research linking higher concentrations of tobacco retailers to increased tobacco use. He 
noted that many Massachusetts municipalities have adopted retailer density regulations and stated 
that reducing retailer clustering supports public health by limiting tobacco exposure in community 
areas.  
 
He discussed research indicating that concentrations of tobacco retailers can increase tobacco use 
and addiction among nearby residents and visitors. He noted that a growing number of 
Massachusetts municipalities have adopted regulations limiting the clustering of tobacco retailers 
and stated that these policies have not been reversed in the communities where they have been 
implemented. Mr. Banthin further stated that reducing retailer clustering promotes equitable public 
health protections by limiting concentrated exposure to tobacco products near residential areas, 
parks, playgrounds, and other community locations.  
 
 City Councilor Gary Rosen spoke in support of the proposed amendments, stating they 
appropriately balance public health protections with support for local small businesses.  He 
reminded the group of his p revious service on the BOH and  expressed support for the proposed
exemptions to the 500 -foot retailer -to-retailer buffer and encouraged the Board to adopt the 
updated regulations. 
 
 Anna Spencer, a resident of Amherst and a UMass preventive medicine resident in public 
health, spoke in support of maintaining the proposed 500-foot separation between tobacco retailers 
and establishments permitting commercial smoking. She stated that reducing tobacco retailer 
density would discourage tobacco use and urged the Board to prioritize public health and safety. 
 
 Dr. Ted Kramer, a pediatric pulmonologist at UMass Memorial Medical Center, spoke in 
opposition to the proposed changes. He testified that children and adolescents are particularly 
vulnerable to nicotine addiction and described the adverse effects of tobacco and vaping exposure, 
including respiratory illness, impaired lung function, and developmental and behavioral impacts. 
Drawing on his clinical experience, he described treating children hospitalized with severe 
respiratory conditions exacerbated by tobacco smoke exposur e. He stated that reducing youth 
exposure to tobacco products can help prevent smoking initiation, and urged the Board to maintain 
regulations that protect children and other vulnerable populations. 
 
 Mark Borenstein, an attorney with Prince Lobel, spoke on behalf of a property owner 
whose tobacco sales permit had lapsed due to family health circumstances. He expressed support 
for the proposed exemption for former permit holders under Section F(1)(c) and urged the Board  
to adopt the regulations as written, noting that the exemption would allow the former permit holder 
the opportunity to obtain a tobacco sales permit again. 
 
 Echo Lewis -Collins, Founder and Executive Director of 508 CHEERS, spoke in 
opposition to the proposed changes. She explained that 508 CHEERS is a Worcester youth 
nonprofit that empowers young people through mentorship, mental health programming, and 
substance use prevention, and noted that she also serves on the Worcester Integrity Task Fo rce. 
She stated that the existing 500 -foot tobacco retailer buffer was created to protect public health, 
prevent the overconcentration of tobacco retailers, and ensure that underserved neighborhoods, 
which have historically been disproportionately impacted  by tobacco use and related health 
disparities, are not burdened further. Drawing on her direct work with young people, she described 
youth vaping as a serious public health concern and said she regularly sees youth navigating 
nicotine addiction, peer pressure, and anxiety in schools, programs, and the community. 
She added that she had joined the Worcester District Attorney’s Office, the Worcester 
Department of Public Health, and Recreation Worcester in educating youth about the dangers of 
vaping and nicotine addiction, underscoring that the city is already investing significant public 
dollars and prevention resources because youth vaping is recognized as a crisis. She urged the 
Board to maintain existing protections, stating that prevention should come before recreation and 
asking whether the Board is trying to protect business convenience or the health and future of 
Worcester’s children.  
 Mike Caine , a Worcester resident representing the Worcester Regional Chamber of 
Commerce, spoke in support of the proposed amendments. He stated that public health and
economic development can coexist, expressed support for responsible tobacco retailers and 
smoking establishments, and raised concerns that the existing 500 -foot buffer could negatively 
impact downtown businesses. He encouraged the Board to adopt regulation s that protect public 
health while supporting compliant local businesses.  
 Anne Bureau , a Worcester resident representing Seven Hills Foundation and the 
Worcester Community Connections Coalition, spoke in opposition to the proposed changes. She 
discussed concerns regarding the health impacts of vaping and nicotine addiction among youth, 
including exposure to harmful chemicals, increased anxiety, mood changes, and potential long -
term health effects. She stated that youth vaping has become a significant concern among 
community organizations, including the Worcester office of the Department of Ch ildren and 
Families. 
Ms. Bureau expressed concern that increasing the number of vaping establishments and 
smoking bars could send a message to youth that tobacco and nicotine use is accepted. She urged 
the Board to prioritize youth health and prevention efforts and maintain th e existing 500 -foot 
buffer policy. 
 
 Dr. Rob Zavoski , Chief Clinical Officer at Family Health Center of Worcester and a 
practicing pediatrician, spoke in opposition to weakening tobacco control measures. He 
emphasized the importance of protecting youth from nicotine addiction and raised concerns about 
flavored tobacco products and marketing strategies that increase youth exposure. Dr. Zavoski 
urged the Board to consider the message that changes to tobacco regulations could send to young 
people and urged the Board to continue prioritizing youth health protections.  
Dr. Zavoski discussed tobacco industry marketing practices, stating that flavored vaping products 
and other strategies are used to attract young people. Drawing from his experience as a 
pediatrician, he described conversations with children about smoking a nd noted that many youth  
do not fully understand the risks of nicotine use and addiction. He emphasized that nicotine 
dependence often begins during adolescence and can have lifelong health consequences. 
 
 Narisha Mensah , a Worcester resident and Project Coordinator for the Central Mass 
Tobacco Free Community Partnership, shared concerns she has heard through her work with 
community organizations across Worcester regarding youth vaping and the impact of flavored 
tobacco products on young people. Ms. Mensah stated that a recent community-based assessment 
conducted with organizations serving Worcester families and youth identified a consistent need 
for stronger prevention efforts, education, and policies that create healthier environments for 
young people.  
She encouraged continued collaboration among the Board, community partners, and 
residents to ensure tobacco prevention efforts remain responsive to the needs of Worcester youth 
and families. 
Chair Anthes invited attendees participating remotely to provide testimony.  
 Cheryl Sbarra , Executive Director and Senior Staff Attorney for the Massachusetts 
Association of Health Boards, provided remote public comment in opposition to weakening the
500-foot buffer requirement. She noted unfavorably that Worcester’s high number of smoking 
establishments compared to other Massachusetts communities and expressed concern that changes 
to the regulation could increase such establishments. She encouraged the Board to consider the 
public health implications of modifying the existing buffer.  
 Alaira, a Worcester-based public health professional working with youth programs spoke 
about the impact of vaping on Worcester youth. She shared concerns regarding youth exposure to 
vaping in schools and community settings and emphasized the importance of considering the long-
term effects of tobacco policies on adolescents. She urged the Board to prioritize youth health 
protections. 
 
5. Closing of Public Hearing 
Chair Anthes asked for a motion to close the public hearing. 
 
Motion: Joseph Kahoro entered a motion to close the public hearing. 
Vote: Unanimously approved by the Board. 
 
The Board then proceeded to discussion and consideration of the proposed tobacco regulations. 
 
6. Board Discussion of Proposed Tobacco Regulations 
❖ Chair Anthes provided an overview of the proposed regulations and the review process, 
which began following a request from Noamesco  to obtain a smoking bar license within 
the existing 500-foot buffer zone. She explained that the Board directed staff to review the 
regulations, resulting in broader revisions beyond the buffer requirement. 
The Chair highlighted that the updated regulations provide greater clarity, consistency, and 
enforcement standards, including defined penalties, training requirements, and 
accountability measures for tobacco retailers. She noted that while certain buffer provisions 
have been modified, the revised regulations continue to address tobacco retailer clustering 
and protect public health. 
Chair Anthes explained that the proposed regulations establish clearer distinctions between 
- smoking bars,  
- retail establishments,  
- and newly defined smoke shops.  
 
She noted that while certain clustering restrictions may be adjusted for smoking bars, 
similar restrictions would remain for tobacco retailers and smoke shops. She stated that the 
revisions are intended to improve clarity, enforcement, education, and accountability while 
addressing public health concerns. 
❖ Board Member Michael Perotto thanked the administration, Chair Anthes, staff, and 
members of the public for their participation. He acknowledged the lengthy review process 
and stated that the proposed regulations balance public health protection with
considerations for local businesses. He highlighted key provisions, including a cap on 
smoke shops/tobacco-focused establishments, clearer regulations to improve enforcement 
consistency, and continued penalties for violations involving sales to individuals under age 
21. 
He further emphasized that youth exposure to tobacco and nicotine products, particularly 
vaping products, remains a significant public health concern. He supported maintaining 
enforcement measures to prevent youth access and stated that the proposed regula tions 
balance public health protection with the legal use of tobacco products by adults. He 
expressed support for moving the regulations forward. 
 
❖ Board Member Patrick Lowe reflected on the Board’s year -long review of the proposed 
regulations and acknowledged the range of perspectives considered, including public 
health concerns and economic impacts on businesses and employees. He stated that the 
revised regulations provide stronger enforcement tools, increase accountability for tobacco 
retailers, and represent a thoughtful balance of community interests. He said the proposed 
regulations represent an important compromise that prioritizes public health while 
recognizing that adult consumption of tobacco products remains legal under state law. The 
speaker noted that the regulations aim to balance public health goals with the economic 
interests of the City. While he supports the  proposed regulations, he expressed hope that 
future discussions may focus on broader tobacco control measures, including potentially a 
statewide ban on future sales of nicotine products. 
❖ Board Member Joseph Kahoro expressed appreciation to the Chair, staff, and especially 
the community members for their work and engagement on the issue. He stated that the 
regulations require balancing public health priorities with the needs of a diverse community 
and supporting local businesses. He clarified that the proposed changes do not increase the 
number of smoking bars, noting that there is an existing cap on the number of licenses and 
the City remains below that limit. He expressed support for the proposed regulations. 
The Chair discussed the Board’s year -long review of the proposed regulations and the balance 
between public health priorities and community and economic considerations. She noted that 
discussions included perspectives on eliminating smoking in Worcester, e mployment concerns 
raised by community members, and the importance of considering the needs of a diverse city. 
Chair Anthes stated that the proposed regulations represent a balanced approach and expressed 
support for their adoption. She highlighted that the regulations provide the Health Department and 
Police Department with additional enforcement tools and stated that the changes should not be 
viewed as a relaxation of tobacco regulations, but rather as increased accountability for toba cco 
retailers. 
7. Motion to Proceed with Vote 
The Chair asked Board members whether they felt sufficient information and public input had 
been received to proceed with a vote on the proposed tobacco regulations. She noted that the Board
had received extensive public testimony and had spent significant time reviewing the regulations 
over the prior year. Board Member Michael Perotto expressed support for proceeding.  
Michael Perotto made a motion  that the Board  move forward with consideration to vote on the 
proposed regulations. 
Effective Date and Implementation Process 
The Chair noted that the effective date for the proposed tobacco regulations would need to be 
included in the motion and asked Nikki Nixon, Interim Director, to provide information on 
implementation and enforcement readiness. Nikki stated that the Division  of Public Health had 
developed standard operating procedures for processing tobacco applications through Open.Gov 
and would ensure a transparent, fair, and consistent process if the regulations were adopted. 
Ms. Nixon explained that, 
• new tobacco applications would be accepted beginning on the effective date of the adopted 
regulations.  
• Applications would be processed on a first-come, first-served basis based on the date and 
time a complete application is received through Open.Gov.  
• Applications must include all required documentation and meet applicable local and state 
requirements before a permit is issued.  
• Applications submitted prior to the effective date would not be considered and would need 
to be resubmitted.  
She stated that this process would ensure a fair, transparent, and consistent permitting process. 
The Chair reiterated that the proposed regulations would not increase the total number of available 
tobacco-related licenses. She explained that currently vacant licenses may become available for 
application upon adoption of the regulations and that applications would only be accepted after the 
effective date on a first-come, first-served basis. 
Board members confirmed their understanding of the implementation process. The Chair stated 
that staff appeared prepared to implement the regulations and proposed an effective date of July 
15, 2026, allowing sufficient time for implementation while ensuring timely enactment. 
Adoption of Tobacco Regulations and Effective Date 
Following discussion and approval of the effective date, the Chair revised the motion to accept the 
proposed tobacco regulations as presented, with an effective date of July 15, 2026. 
 
The Board voted as follows: 
• Joseph Corr – Yes 
• Patrick Lowe – Yes 
• Michael Perotto – Yes 
• Frances Anthes – Yes
The motion passed unanimously.  
 
The Chair announced that the Board had adopted the updated City of Worcester Tobacco 
Regulations and thanked all participants for their time and input throughout the process. 
 
8. Adjournment 
The Chair asked if there was any additional business to come before the Board. Hearing none, she 
requested a motion to adjourn. 
A motion to adjourn was made by Michael Perotto. The Board voted as follows: 
• Michael Perotto – Yes 
• Joseph Kahoro – Yes 
• Patrick Lowe – Yes 
• Frances Anthes – Yes 
The motion passed unanimously, and the meeting was adjourned at 7:35 p.m. 
The Chair reminded members that the next Board of Health meeting would be held on August 3, 
2026, at 6:30 PM.
Worcester Board of Health 
Tobacco Regulations  
 
WHEREAS, the Board of Health (“BOH”) of the City of Worcester  (“City”) is charged with 
the regulation and oversight of retail tobacco establishments pursuant to the authority 
granted by Chapter 120 of the Acts of 2014 and Article Six of the Home Rule Charter; and  
 
WHEREAS, the City Council of Worcester has enacted the Tobacco Products Control 
Ordinance, pursuant to Chapter 8, § 3 of the General Revised Ordinances of 2008, to 
protect and promote public health through regulation of the sale of tobacco products; and 
 
WHEREAS, there exists conclusive evidence that tobacco smoking causes cancer, respiratory 
and cardiac diseases, negative birth outcomes, irritations to the eyes, nose, and throat1; and 
 
WHEREAS, the majority (90%) of smokers begin smoking before the age of 25, and over 5 
million youth and young adults (ages 25 and under) smoke2; and  
WHEREAS, the Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection has classified liquid 
nicotine in any amount as an “acutely hazardous waste”; 3  and 
WHEREAS, the density of tobacco retailers near adolescents’ homes has been associated with 
increased youth smoking rates and initiation of non-cigarette tobacco product use4; and 
WHEREAS, tobacco retailers are more prevalent in underserved communities, especially in 
neighborhoods with a higher proportion of African American or Hispanic residents;5 
WHEREAS, policies to reduce tobacco retailer density have been shown to be effective and 
can reduce or eliminate social and racial inequities in the location and distribution of tobacco 
retailers6; and

WHEREAS, the Board of Health has determined that updated regulations are necessary and 
appropriate to realize the protection and promotion of public health while also balancing 
the business demands of a growing city; and  
 
 WHEREAS, the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court has held that “. . . [t]he right to engage 
in business must yield to the paramount right of government to protect the public health 
by any rational means”; 7 and 
WHEREAS, these regulations aim to reduce tobacco use by prioritizing prevention, cessation 
support, and youth protection, while improving public health outcomes and providing 
local businesses with the opportunity to engage in retail tobacco sales; and 
WHEREAS, it is the intention of the Board of Health to regulate the sale of tobacco products; 
NOW THEREFORE, pursuant to the authority granted to Worcester Board of Health by  
M.G.L. c.111, §31, and the requirements set forth in Chapter 8, § 3, of the General  
Revised Ordinances related to Tobacco, the Worcester Board of Health hereby repeals the Board 
of Health Regulations related to  Restricting the Sale of Tobacco Products, effective September 1, 
2016, Restricting the sale of Cigars and Flavored  Tobacco Products, effective January 1, 2019, 
and, Restricting the Number of Tobacco Product Sales Permits, effective October 23, 202 3, and 
replaces said regulations with the following updated regulations. All other existing Board of Health 
Regulations shall remain effective.   
 
 
A. DEFINITIONS  
For the purpose of this regulation (“Regulations”), the definitions found in M.G.L. Chapter 
270 and other applicable state laws, Chapter 8, § 3(b) of the General Revised Ordinances of 
Worcester shall apply, in addition the following words shall have the following meanings. 
 
Blunt Wrap:  Any product made wholly or in part from a tobacco product, manufactured or 
packaged with loose and removable leaves or section of a leaf, or as a hollow tube, which may be 
used by the consumer to wrap or contain loose tobacco or other fillers.  
Electronic Nicotine Delivery System: An electronic device, whether for 1 -time use or reusable, 
that can be used to deliver nicotine or another substance to a person inhaling from the device 
including, but not limited to, electronic cigarettes, electronic cigars, electronic cigarillos, electronic 
pipes, vaping pens, hookah pens and other similar systems that rely on vaporization or 
aerosolization. “Electronic nicotine delivery system” shall also include any noncombustible liquid 
or gel that is manufactured into a finished product for use in such electronic device. “Electronic

(2020) (doi: 10.2105/AJPH.2019.305512); A.E. Myers et al., A comparison of three policy approaches for tobacco 
retailer reduction, 74 Prev. Med. 67(2015) (doi: 10.1016/j.ypmed.2015.01.025).  
7 Druzik et al v. Board of Health of Haverhill, 324 Mass. 129 (1949).
3 
nicotine delivery system” shall also include any component, part, or accessory of a device used 
during the operation of the device even if the part or accessory was sold separately. “Electronic 
nicotine delivery system” shall not include a product that has been approved by the United States 
Food and Drug Administration for sale or use as a tobacco cessation product or for other medical 
purposes and that is marketed and sold or prescribed exclusively for that approved purpose.  
Flavored tobacco product:  Any tobacco product or component part thereof that contains a 
constituent that has or produces a characterizing flavor.  A public statement, claim or indicia made 
or disseminated by the manufacturer of a tobacco product, or by any person authorized or permitted 
by the manufacturer to make or disseminate public statements concerning such tobacco product, 
that such tobacco product has or produces a characterizing flavor shall constitute presumptive 
evidence that the tobacco product is a flavored tobacco product. 
Minimum Legal Sales Age (MLSA): The age an individual must be before that individual  
can be sold a tobacco product in the City.   
 
Minor: Any individual under the age of 21. 
 
Permit: The Tobacco Product Sales Permit issued by the board of health pursuant to this 
regulation. 
Permit Holder: Any person engaged in the sale or distribution of tobacco products that applies 
for and receives a Tobacco Product Sales Permit, or any person that is required to apply for a 
Tobacco Product Sales Permit, or his or her business agent. 
 
Person: Any individual, firm, partnership, association, corporation, company or organization of 
any kind, including but not limited to, an owner, operator, manager, proprietor or person in 
charge of any establishment, business or retail store. 
 
Retailer: Any person or entity that owns, operates, or manages an establishment engaged in the 
sale or distribution of tobacco products, including but not limited to convenience stores, gas 
stations, liquor stores, and other similar businesses. 
 
Schools: Public or private elementary and secondary schools. 
 
Smoke Shop (also known as “Adult-only Retail Tobacco Store” in G.L. c. 270): An 
establishment that is not adjoined, whose only purpose is to sell or offer for retail sale tobacco 
products and/or tobacco product paraphernalia, in which the entry of persons under the age of 21 
is prohibited at all times, and which maintains a valid permit for the retail sale of tobacco 
products from the Worcester Board of Health and applicable state licenses. The establishment 
shall not allow anyone under the age of 21 to work at the establishment.
4 
Smoking Bar: an establishment that: (i) exclusively occupies an enclosed indoor space and is 
primarily engaged in the retail sale of tobacco products for consumption by customers on the 
premises; (ii) derives revenue from the sale of food, alcohol or other beverages that is incidental 
to the sale of a tobacco product and prohibits entry to a person under 21 years of age; (iii) 
prohibits a food or beverage not sold directly by the establishment from being consumed on the 
premises; (iv) maintains a valid permit for the retail sale of a tobacco product as required to be 
issued by the Worcester Board of Health; and (v) maintains a valid permit issued by the 
Massachusetts Department of Revenue to operate as a Smoking Bar. “Smoking Bar” shall 
include, but is not limited to, those establishments that are commonly known as “cigar bars” and 
“hookah bars.” 
Tobacco Product: Any product containing, made, or derived from tobacco or nicotine that is 
intended for human consumption, whether smoked, chewed, absorbed, dissolved, inhaled, vaped, 
snorted, sniffed, or ingested by any other means, including, but not limited to: cigarettes, cigars, 
little cigars, chewing tobacco, pipe tobacco, snuff, or electronic cigarettes, electronic cigars, 
electronic pipes, electronic hookah, or other similar products, regardless of nicotine content, that 
rely on vaporization or aerosolization. “Tobacco product” includes any component or part of a 
tobacco product. “Tobacco product” does not include any product that has been approved by the 
United States Food and Drug Administration either as a tobacco use cessation product or for 
other medical purposes and which is being marketed and sold or prescribed solely for the 
approved purpose. 
Tobacco Product Flavor Enhancer: Any product designed, manufactured, produced, marketed, 
or sold to produce a characterizing flavor when added to any tobacco product. 
 
B. TOBACCO SALES TO PERSONS UNDER THE MINIMUM LEGAL SALES AGE 
PROHIBITED 
 
1. The minimum legal sales age in the city of Worcester is twenty-one (21).   
 
2. No Retailer shall sell or otherwise distribute a tobacco product to a minor. 
 
3. Required signage: Retailers who sell or permit the sale of tobacco products shall comply 
with applicable local and state signage requirements, including but not limited to those 
required in M.G.L. c. 270 and 105 CMR 665.015. Retailers shall conspicuously post 
signage provided by the City that discloses current referral information about smoking 
cessation. 
 
4. All Smoking Bars and Smoke Shops shall post signage, in the form developed and made 
available by the City, on the exterior of the door providing entrance to the Smoke Shop or 
Smoking Bar and such sign shall not be obstructed from view or placed at a height of less 
than four feet or greater than nine from the bottom of the door. Such signage
5 
shall state that "No person younger than 21 years old is permitted on the premises at any 
time.”  
 
5.  All Smoking Bars and Smoke Shops that allow for any onsite consumption of tobacco 
products shall post signage, in the form developed and made available by the City, on the 
exterior of the door providing entrance to the Smoke Shop or Smoking Bar and such sign 
shall not be obstructed from view or placed at a height of less than four feet or greater 
than nine from the bottom of the door. Such signage shall warn persons entering that 
smoking and vaping may be present on the premises and provide information concerning 
the health risks associated with secondhand smoke and the use of tobacco products, 
including electronic nicotine delivery systems.    
 
6. Retailers shall conspicuously post a sign stating that “The sale of tobacco products, 
including e-cigarettes, to anyone under the age of 21 years is prohibited.”  The notice 
shall be no smaller than 8.5 inches by 11 inches and shall be posted conspicuously in the 
retail establishment or other place in such a manner so that they may be readily seen by a 
person standing at or approaching the cash register. The notice shall directly face the 
purchaser and shall not be obstructed from view or placed at a height of less than four (4) 
feet or greater than nine (9) feet from the floor.   
 
7.  Identification: Each Retailer selling or distributing tobacco products shall verify the age 
of the purchaser by means of valid government-issued photographic identification 
showing the purchaser is not a minor. Verification is required for any person under the 
age of twenty-seven.   
 
8. All retail sales of tobacco products, as defined herein, must be face-to-face between the 
seller and the buyer and occur at the permitted location. 
 
9. No person shall sell or otherwise distribute tobacco products within the City of  
Worcester without first obtaining a Tobacco Product Sales Permit issued annually by the 
Board of Health. Only owners of establishments with a permanent, non-mobile location 
in Worcester are eligible to apply for a permit and sell tobacco products at a specified 
location in Worcester.   
 
C. PROHIBITIONS  
 
1. No Retailer may sell or distribute any cigarette package that contains fewer than twenty 
cigarettes, including single cigarettes. 
 
2. Self-service displays of tobacco products are prohibited. All humidors including, but not 
limited to, walk-in humidors must be locked. The only exception is self-service displays that 
are located in facilities where the Retailer ensures that no minor is present, or permitted to 
enter, at any time.  
 
3. Tobacco vending machines are prohibited.
6 
4. Non-Residential Roll-Your-Own machines are prohibited. 
 
5. No health care provider, institutional or non-institutional, shall sell tobacco products or allow 
tobacco products to be sold on its premises.  No retail establishment that operates, maintains, 
or employs a health care provider within it, such as a pharmacy or drug store, shall sell 
tobacco products or cause tobacco products to be sold. 
 
6. No educational institution shall sell or allow tobacco products to be sold on its premises.  
This includes all educational institutions as well as any retail establishments that operate on 
the property of an educational institution. 
 
7. The sale or distribution of tobacco products in any building or facility owned or operated by 
the City shall be prohibited, except as authorized by the City Council. 
 
8. No Retailer shall: 
a)  Distribute any free samples of tobacco products; 
b) Accept or redeem any coupon that provides any tobacco product without charge or for 
less than the listed or non-discounted price; 
c) Sell a tobacco product to consumers through any multi-pack discounts (e.g., "buy-two-
get-one-free") or otherwise provide or distribute to consumers any tobacco product 
without charge or for less than the listed or non-discounted price in exchange for the 
purchase of any other tobacco product; 
d) Sell or cause to be sold blunt wrap; 
e) Sell or distribute tobacco products in any form other than an original factory-wrapped 
package, including the repackaging or dispensing of any tobacco product for retail sale. 
 
9. No person shall sell or distribute or cause to be sold or distributed any flavored tobacco 
product, as defined herein, except in Smoking Bars for on-site consumption only. 
 
10. No person shall sell an electronic nicotine delivery system with nicotine content greater than 
35 milligrams per milliliter; provided, however, that this subsection shall not apply to S moke 
Shops and Smoking Bars for sampling and on-site consumption, respectively. 
 
11. Retailers who sell Liquid Nicotine Containers must comply with the provisions of 310 CMR 
30.000, Massachusetts Hazardous Waste Regulations.  
 
 
D. CIGAR SALES 
 
1. No person shall sell or distribute a single cigar unless such cigar is priced for retail sale at two 
dollars and fifty cents ($2.50) or more. 
2. No person shall sell or distribute any original factory-wrapped package of two or more cigars, 
unless such package is priced for retail sale at five dollars ($5.00) or more.
7 
3. This section shall not apply to a person or entity engaged in the business of selling or 
distributing cigars for commercial purposes. 
4. The BOH reserves the right to amend these prices from time to time.  
 
E. RETAIL TOBACCO PERMIT REQUIREMENTS 
 
1. As part of the Tobacco Product Sales Permit application and renewal process, all applicants 
will be provided with these BOH Tobacco Regulations through the permitting system. Each 
applicant is required to electronically sign a statement declaring that they have read the 
Regulations and acknowledge responsibility for instructing all employees who will be 
involved in tobacco product sales on all applicable federal, state, and local laws, as well as 
these Regulations.  
 
2. No permit holder shall allow an employee to sell tobacco products until the employee 
acknowledges, in writing, receipt of the Regulations, Ordinance, and applicable state, a copy 
of which will be placed on file in the office of the employer and made available to the BOH, 
or its designee, upon request.  
 
3. Applicants shall provide proof of a current tobacco sales license issued by the Massachusetts 
Department of Revenue before a local permit may be issued.  
 
4. Issuance of permits shall be conditioned on an applicant’s consent to unannounced, periodic 
inspections of the retail establishment to ensure compliance with these Regulations and all 
applicable laws and regulations.  
 
5. Permits shall be issued annually and shall be valid for one calendar year beginning on the 
first day of January and ending on the thirty-first day of December. Permits are renewable 
annually to the same permit holder each year by the thirty-first day of December, upon 
submittal of an application in compliance with these Regulations and the applicable 
Ordinance. Any permit holder that fails to renew a permit by the thirty-first day of December 
and continues to operate shall be subject to penalty and enforcement under these Regulations. 
 
6. A separate permit is required for each retail establishment selling tobacco products.  
 
7. Permits shall be displayed at the retail establishment in a conspicuous location and consistent 
with these Regulations.  
 
8. Permit holders shall have no property interest in any permit issued hereunder.   
 
9. A permit will not be renewed if the permit holder has outstanding fines, penalties or fees due 
to the city of Worcester for any reason unless such fines, penalties or fees are the subject of a 
lawful and pending legal appeal.
8 
10. A permit will not be renewed or transferred if the permit holder has sold a tobacco product to 
a minor three (3) times within the previous twenty-four (24) months and any appeal periods 
have expired for any such violation.   
 
 
F. MAXIMUM NUMBER OF TOBACCO PRODUCT SALES PERMITS  
 
1. At any given time, there shall be no more than two hundred thirty-five (235) Tobacco 
Product Sales Permits, twenty-two (22) of which may be issued to Smoke Shops, and fifteen 
(15) of which shall be issued to Smoking Bars pursuant to Section 3(e) of Chapter 8 of the 
General Revised Ordinances and M.G.L c. 270.   
 
a) There shall be no more than twenty-two (22) Smoke Shop Permits issued in Worcester. 
 
b) Density.  A new Retail Tobacco Product Sales Permit shall not be issued to an applicant 
within five hundred (500) feet of an existing Retail Tobacco Product Sales Permit or an 
existing public or private elementary or secondary school as measured in a straight line 
from the nearest point of the property line of the school to the nearest point of the 
property line of the retail establishment.  
 
c) Exemption. Applications for a Retail Tobacco Product Sales Permit at a location which  
held a Retail Tobacco Product Sales Permit within the previous three (3) years as of the 
effective date of this Regulation shall be exempt from the Retail to Retail 500-foot buffer. 
This exemption is applicable to the Retail to Retail 500-foot density regulation. No other 
exemption of these Regulations, including of the 235 total Tobacco Product Sales Permit 
cap, shall be permitted. 
 
2. Transfer of Permits.   
a) Applicants who purchase or acquire an existing business that holds a valid Tobacco 
Product Sales Permit at the time of the sale or acquisition shall apply, within sixty (60) 
days of such sale or acquisition, for a transfer of the permit, in accordance with these 
Regulations and any applicable local and state rules and regulations.  
b) Permits may be transferred incident to the relocation of a retail establishment by the 
existing permit holder. Permit transfer requests may be made in writing to the Worcester 
Division of Public Health with the requested change in license address. A new permit 
may be issued if the new location complies with all requirements of these Regulations 
including density requirements, and any applicable state rules and regulations, including 
outstanding penalties, are satisfied in full.
9 
3. Smoking Bars Regulated. 
a) There shall be no more than fifteen (15) Smoking Bar Permits issued in Worcester. 
 
b) Any permit holder, or new Applicant, who fails to renew/transfer their Permit, within 
sixty (60) days of the expiration, or purchase of a business, shall be treated as a first-time 
applicant.  
 
c) Density.  A new Smoking Bar Permit shall not be issued to an applicant within five 
hundred (500) feet of an existing public or private elementary or secondary school as 
measured in a straight line from the nearest point of the property line of the school to the 
nearest point of the property line of the establishment. 
 
G.  INCORPORATION OF STATE LAWS AND REGULATIONS 
The sale or distribution of the products defined herein must comply with those provisions 
found at General Laws, Chapter 270, §§ 6-7, and 27-29 and Chapter 112, §61A. Further, the 
sale or distribution of tobacco products  must comply with state regulations including but not 
limited to those provisions found at 940 CMR 21.00, Sale and Distribution of Cigarettes, 
Smokeless Tobacco Products, and Electronic Smoking Devices in Massachusetts, 940 CMR 
22.00 Sale and Distribution of Cigars in Massachusetts; and 105 CMR 665.00, Minimum 
Standards for Retail Sale of Tobacco and Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems , and all 
applicable state, local and federal laws and regulations. 
H. VIOLATIONS 
Fines, Penalties and Enforcement Authority. Enforcement of this Regulation shall be by the 
Worcester Board of Health or its designated agent(s), including employees of the Department 
of Health and Human Services, the Worcester Police Department, and any authorized agent 
or officer of the city of Worcester on any public property, on any private property which 
is subject to a permit required by these Regulations or any private property which is open 
to public use.  
This Regulation may be enforced by civil process, criminal process or by non- criminal 
disposition as provided in General Laws, Chapter 40, § 21D, and further, where applicable, 
as set forth in General Laws, Chapter 270, §§28 and 29. Every day, or part thereof, in which 
any person is in violation of these Regulations, or any applicable Ordinance, shall constitute 
a single and separate offense.  
Permit Holders are required to comply with any and all local, state and federal laws and 
regulations and any violation of such shall be grounds for the BOH to modify, suspend or 
revoke a permit. In addition to the monetary fines and penalties described herein, any 
person who violates any provisions of  these Regulations shall be  subject to  the 
suspension, modification or revocation of  the Tobacco Product Sales Permit issued by the 
BOH.
10 
a) Consistent with 105 CMR 665.055, the BOH may, after written notice to a Retailer, which 
notice shall contain the reasons therefore and establish a time and date for a hearing , 
modify, suspend or revoke a Tobacco Product Sales Permit, upon satisfactory proof that a 
violation of any law or regulation of the Board of Health, the city of Worcester, or of the 
Commonwealth has occurred. The Retailer shall have an opportunity to be heard at such 
hearing and shall be notified in writing of the BOH’s decision and the reasons therefore in 
writing.   
 
b) For violations of the sections of these Regulations that incorporate G.L. c. 270, §§6, 28, 29 
and 105 CMR 665.000, the following penalties shall apply:  
i. In the case of a first violation, a fine of one thousand dollars ($1,000.00) for a 
State Law violation shall be issued and, if the violation is the  sale of a tobacco 
product to a Minor the Tobacco Product Sales Permit shall be suspended for 
three (3) consecutive business days;  
ii. In the case of a second violation within thirty- six (36) months of the date of a  
previous violation, a fine of two thousand dollars ($2,000.00) for a State Law 
violation shall be issued and the Tobacco Product Sales Permit shall  be 
suspended for seven (7) consecutive business days;  
iii. In the case of three or more violations within a thirty- six (36)-month period, a 
fine of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) for a State Law violation shall be 
issued and the Tobacco Product Sales Permit shall be suspended for thirty (30) 
consecutive business days. 
 c) For all other violations specific to local regulations and ordinances, the following penalties 
shall apply:  
 
i. In the case of a first violation, a fine of three hundred dollars ($300);  
 
ii. In the case of a second violation within thirty -six (36) months of a  previous 
violation, a fine of four hundred dollars ($400) and the Tobacco Product Sales 
Permit shall be suspended for 7 consecutive business days;  
 
iii. In the case of t hree or more violations within thirty -six (36) months , a fine of 
five hundred dollars ($5 00) and the Tobacco Product Sales Permit shall  be 
suspended for thirty (30) consecutive business days. 
 
d) In the case of four (4) or more violations or repeated, egregious violations of these 
Regulations or any applicable local or state law or r egulation, within a 36 month period, 
the BOH may hold a hearing in accordance with these Regulations and 105 CMR 665.000, 
and after such hearing, permanently modify or revoke the tobacco permit.  
 
 
e) Fraud, misrepresentation, false material statement, concealment, or suppression of the facts 
by a permit holder  in connection with an application, or renewal,  for a T obacco Product 
Sales Permit shall be grounds for denial or revocation of a permit.
